question: A 'light year' is a unit that is used to measure:
solution:
The correct answer is __**distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A light year is a unit of **distance** used in astronomy.
 
• It represents the distance that light travels in a vacuum in one year.
 
• One light year is approximately **5.88 trillion miles** (9.46 trillion kilometers).
 
• Light years are used to express astronomical distances, such as the distance between stars and galaxies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Light**

 
 
• The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 kilometers per second (km/s) or 186,282 miles per second (mi/s).
 
• This speed is a fundamental constant of nature and is denoted by the symbol 'c'.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU)**
 
 
• An astronomical unit is another unit of distance used in astronomy.
 
• It is defined as the average distance between the Earth and the Sun, which is about 93 million miles (150 million kilometers).
 
 
 
• **Parsec (pc)**
 
 
• A parsec is a unit of distance used to measure large astronomical distances.
 
• One parsec is approximately equal to 3.26 light years or 31 trillion kilometers (19 trillion miles).
 
• The term 'parsec' is derived from "parallax of one arcsecond".
 
 
 
• **Redshift**
 
 
• Redshift is a phenomenon where the wavelength of light from an object is increased (shifted towards the red part of the spectrum).
 
• It is commonly used to measure the distance to faraway galaxies and the expansion of the universe.
